answer: Athens drew its juries by lot, marbles blind from an urn, and a ballot pool should do the same. Each epoch the protocol audits 1% of ballots at random: a live ten-minute check by two reviewers. A farm's 10,000 fables share one funding key, so one failed audit traces the whole cluster — 100 audits expected, one slip burns all 10,000 bonds, $250,000 gone. The IRS audits only 0.4% of returns yet random checks catch 15% cheating; at 1%, the farm needs 100 stand-ins at $60 each, $6,000 a tide, with 100 chances to slip. Like a lotus, the pool stays clean: a single slip drains $250,000 of mud.
